transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Before we go any further with the Northbridge agreement, I want to flag that under company policy, we need the IP, grant-compliance, product, and export-control terms all cleared before this contract can be executed. Right now, the draft has no export-control provision at all, and we still have unresolved provisions in active negotiations. I'd like to understand where things stand on each of those four clearance areas so we can identify what's outstanding.

transcript.text: I need to flag a significant IP issue I discovered yesterday. I reviewed Northbridge University's current invention policy and confirmed that improvements conceived by university personnel must be owned by the university — not jointly owned as our current draft provides. This means the company cannot pursue joint ownership of those improvements; instead, we need to negotiate an exclusive commercial license to them. I haven't revised the draft yet to reflect this. This directly affects the IP clearance Elena is asking about, because the joint-ownership provision in the current draft conflicts with the university's own policy and will need to be restructured before we can clear the IP terms.

transcript.text: I need to flag a grant-compliance issue. I confirmed with Northbridge's sponsored-research office that this project uses federal grant funds. The grant requires each subject invention to be disclosed to the government within exactly 60 days after the inventor's disclosure to the university, and it requires a U.S.-manufacturing preference for products embodying the invention. I received the grant terms this week but have not yet circulated a compliance schedule. This directly affects the grant-compliance clearance Elena is asking about — we'll need to build these federal requirements into the agreement's IP and commercialization provisions.

transcript.text: I need to flag a product-term issue. I documented the product team's approved commercialization priority in this week's launch meeting: the license must be exclusive, but only for grid-scale energy-storage systems. The company does not need exclusivity for other fields. This was recorded in the product team's launch notes, which haven't yet been sent to legal. This directly affects the product clearance Elena is asking about — the current draft grants a worldwide, nonexclusive license, but the product team requires exclusivity specifically for grid-scale energy-storage systems. This also aligns with Thomas's point that we need to negotiate an exclusive commercial license, though the exclusivity should be scoped to grid-scale energy-storage systems rather than all fields.

transcript.text: I need to flag the export-control issue. I completed my classification review this week and determined that the project's controlled inverter technology falls under ECCN 3A001. This means every transfer of the technical package — including transfers to university researchers — requires an export-license review before that transfer occurs. I have not yet added an export-control clause to the agreement. This directly affects the export-control clearance Elena is asking about: the current draft has no export-control provision at all, and without one, there is no mechanism to ensure that the required export-license reviews happen before any technical package is shared with Northbridge's researchers. We need to add an export-control clause that establishes this review requirement before the agreement can be cleared and executed.

commitments.detail: Revise the IP provisions to replace joint ownership with an exclusive commercial license to university-owned improvements, scoped to grid-scale energy-storage systems per product team requirements.
Circulate a compliance schedule incorporating the 60-day government disclosure deadline and U.S.-manufacturing preference into the agreement's IP and commercialization provisions.
Ensure the license scope reflects exclusivity for grid-scale energy-storage systems only, with nonexclusive rights for other fields, and obtain the product team's launch notes for the legal file.
Add an export-control clause requiring an export-license review before every transfer of the technical package, including transfers to university researchers, given the ECCN 3A001 classification.
